Subject: EU-only processing: need operational evidence and deletion timeline

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Medix Health is proceeding with a security review for our planned pilot (PHI-sensitive inference). Our board counsel has two high-priority asks before we can sign: 

1) Evidence that inference workloads and any derived outputs for our tenant are processed and stored only within the EU (including backups and any KV caches).
2) A clear, auditable deletion playbook (timeline, evidence artifacts, and proof of deletion) for customer data and cached state.

Also: we need to understand how SCCs apply here (we're evaluating Schrems II exposure), and whether we can get an attestation around KMS key residency/ownership for any in-region keys.

Can you send an operational bundle we can share with legal? If there are gaps, please call them out and propose mitigations.

Would prefer a short read (1-2 pages) + supporting artifacts.

Best,
Emma Jones
Data Protection Officer
Medix Health

--

Hi Emma / team,

Below is a focused summary of the operational posture and the evidence artifacts we can provide. I'll attach the diagrams and the retention/deletion playbook.

Operational posture (short):
- Inference compute: staffed inference clusters in our Frankfurt and Paris regions only for customers that choose EU-only processing. Requests are routed to in-region pools and never leave the region for inference execution.
- Data at rest: model inputs, output tokens, and intermediate KV cache are stored on region-local volumes. Backups are scheduled and stored in the same region(s); we do not replicate backups to non-EU regions for EU-only tenants.
- Control plane: customer metadata (account IDs, billing) resides in our control plane; for EU-only tenants we offer a private control plane option (VPC) where control plane elements can be configured to sit in the EU. If a customer remains on the hosted control plane, we provide documented contractual limits and SCCs mapping.
- KMS keys: we can support a customer-managed key (CMK) in an EU KMS (Cloud provider KMS or on-prem HSM). We also provide an in-region KMS ownership statement for cases where Redwood manages keys but keeps them in-region.
- Operator access & audit: role-based access enforced with just-in-time approval for escalations. All operator sessions are logged with session recordings and command audit logs (we can provide redacted samples).

Evidence artifacts we will include:
- eu-inference-ops-flow.png (ops/data flow diagram)
- dtia-summary.pdf (high-level Data Transfer Impact Assessment summary)
- sccs-extract.docx (mapping of SCCs clauses to Redwood obligations + our transfer chain map)
- kms-key-ownership-statement.pdf (statement of key residency/ownership for in-region keys)
- deletion-playbook.md (step-by-step erasure + forensic checks)
- sample audit logs (redacted) — available on request with NDA redaction rules applied

Open items / caveats:
- If you require the control plane fully in-region under your tenancy, we'll need to scope a Private deployment (timelines and cost differ).
- For hosted customers, SCCs + DTIA combination is how we reduce transfer risk; we can provide a signed attestation but note it references the hosted-control-plane topology unless you opt for private.

I'll attach the artifacts to this thread. Happy to jump on the call Friday and walk through.

— Naomi
Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference

Emma — quick legal note on SCCs and attestation options: 

- SCCs (standard contractual clauses) remain the primary contractual mechanism to lawfully transfer data where needed. For customers needing a stronger limit on transfer risk, we recommend combining SCCs with a DTIA and technical mitigations (in-region processing, KMS residency, no cross-border backups).
- We can provide a signed attestation summarizing the specific protections applied to Medix Health (will cite the artifacts Naomi is assembling). That attestation will include: list of regions used, KMS residency statement (if applicable), backup policy, and operator access constraints.
- If Medix requires the control plane and telemetry to be in the EU under Redwood-managed infrastructure, we will need to move to a Private deployment (we've provided indicative pricing previously).

Next steps I propose: 
1) Redwood prepares an evidence bundle and a draft attestation (legal).
2) Medix reviews and requests any clarifying artifacts.
3) If Medix needs a legally binding amendment (SLA/contract line) to guarantee in-region control plane, we engage procurement/legal to schedule a redline.

I will prepare a short SCCs mapping doc and initiate a DocuSign packet for the attestation so it can be signed once the bundle is complete.

— Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks — a couple of clarifications from our side before the call: 
- Deletion timeline: for emergency erasure requests (regulatory), we need a maximum time-to-erasure for cached state and backups and a forensic proof artifact (hash + timestamped deletion log). Is that something you can provide within 24 hours of a request?
- KMS: we prefer customer-managed KMS keys held in our EU subscription; will Redwood allow us to bring our own CMK and prevent Redwood from exporting key material?

If yes to both, we can proceed to finalize the pilot timeline. Otherwise we'll need to understand risk mitigations.

Emma / Tom — thanks for the clarifying questions. Quick answers and next steps: 

- Deletion timeline: our deletion-playbook.md documents typical SLOs. For cached state (KV cache + inference artifacts) we can execute an emergency purge and return a timestamped deletion log and SHA256 hash of the erased snapshot within 24 hours for EU-only tenants on Private or Dedicated offerings. For hosted EU-only tenants we can meet 48-hour SLO for a full forensic artifact; we'll include the specific runbook in the bundle.
- KMS/CMK: yes, you can bring your own CMK in an EU-managed KMS subscription. Redwood will not export key material; we support envelope encryption with your CMK anchoring the DEKs. We'll attach the kms-key-ownership-statement.pdf with the exact mechanics.

Attachments included in this thread: eu-inference-ops-flow.png, dtia-summary.pdf, sccs-extract.docx, kms-key-ownership-statement.pdf, deletion-playbook.md
